# syntax-chain-payloads: an opaque value inside each position a widened syntax reading takes for
# structure: a macro or attribute name, an attribute item, a member after a closure parameter or a
# tuple field, a go type assertion, map key or package-qualified element type, a generic
# argument of an open call, a labelled argument read from its enclosing call, a call ended by a
# quote and a lone type name marked optional. the reading must judge the value it claims, so each
# line stays reported. chunked and sub-20-byte values, which the placeholder grammar cannot
# express, are generated at run time in tests/syntax_montecarlo_tests.rs.

generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE={S32}!(value)
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=#![{S32}]
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=#[derive({S32})]
generic-high-entropy-value	        #expect({S32}.{S36})
generic-high-entropy-value	        #expect(0x{HEX32})
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=@AppStorage({B64_44})
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=$0.{S32}.count
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=self.0.{S36}
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=value.(*{S32})
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=map[{S32}]int{}
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=[]pkg.{S40}{value}

generic-high-entropy-value	setting="make(for: {S32})"
generic-high-entropy-value	setting="make(for: {S32}.{S36})"
